PARTIAL_HEAD = 200
# The curator's short block ids, `[#<12 hex>]` (GH #892), which a history tool's
# result quotes by design. The digest goes to a READER, straight past the
# splitter that takes them out of a model's prose, so it takes them out here --
# the same expression, by form alone (GH #894, R-27-3: internal block ids never
# leave the colony, OR-KY-68) -- a history tool answers in JSON and writes its
# ids BARE, `"id": "#<12 hex>"`, so the bare form and the window's forms of a
# released or expired block come out as well (OR-KY-80), up to the sixteen
# digits of an ambiguous id's `candidates` (OR-KY-81) and the sixty-four of a
# `history_read` answer's `hash` (OR-KY-84); a free-standing run needs a letter
# a-f, so an order number stays. One expression with the splitter's, held byte
# for byte by a lock (OR-KY-83). The raw round in front
# of it keeps them.
SHORT_ID = re.compile(
    r"[ \t]?(?:\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?: released[^\]\n]{0,64}| expired)?\]"
    r"|\[shortened[^\]\n#]{0,40}#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}[^\]\n]{0,4}\]"
    r"|\(#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}\)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#(?=[0-9]{0,15}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?!\w)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#?(?=[0-9]{0,63}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{64}(?!\w))")


def partial_answer_turn(thread, names):
    """The NAMED end of a capped round (GH #570).

    A round that spends its iteration budget used to leave on the answer lane
    with the raw end of the tool round as its last turn -- and the last turn is
    precisely what a consumer reads (`any_text` above, and every surface built
    on it). Measured on e18: a core capped mid-search, its answer ended on a
    `web_search` result, and the person was shown the search payload. The better
    the errand was going, the more certainly a tool got quoted at the reader.

    So the round says what happened to it, in one assistant turn: the bound it
    hit, how many calls it made, which tools it called, and the head of the last
    result. Nothing is lost by it -- the raw round travels in the same message,
    in front of it; what changes is the LAST word.

    Deterministic by construction: names in call order, deduplicated; the last
    result without the short block ids it quotes (GH #894), whitespace-collapsed
    and cut to PARTIAL_HEAD. No model, no clock.

    The names come from `thread_of`'s own `names` map (call id -> tool name),
    which is built while the rounds are read. Parsing the `function` object a
    second time here would be a second reader of the same declaration, and the
    two could disagree.
    """
    calls, called, last = 0, [], ""
    for x in thread:
        if not isinstance(x, dict):
            continue
        if x.get("type") == "tool_call":
            calls += 1
            nm = str(names.get(str(x.get("id") or ""), "") or "")
            if nm and nm not in called:
                called.append(nm)
        elif x.get("type") == "tool_result":
            last = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
    if not calls:
        return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                "text": PARTIAL_ANSWER_EMPTY % MAX_ITER}
    head_ = " ".join(SHORT_ID.sub("", last).split())[:PARTIAL_HEAD]
    text = PARTIAL_ANSWER % (MAX_ITER, calls,
                             ", ".join(called) or "unnamed",
                             head_ or "(nothing)")
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "text", "text": text}


def curate_message(rows, nxt):
    """The ONE seam. Everything the agent LLM is going to see of this round
    leaves through this message and no other: the opening turn(s), the tool
    round, the memory and the brief pair -- whole, and nothing of an earlier
    round, because the curator behind `curate` owns the window (R-27-1,
    GH #889).

    It is also where the round ENDS (GH #77). A turn that has spent its
    iteration budget leaves on the ANSWER lane with everything it collected
    instead of asking the brain again, and says so with round_capped=1. The
    round begins at the seam, so nothing downstream is ever needed to stop it.

    Since 3.5.0 it also ends on a SENTENCE (GH #570): the spent branch appends
    the partial answer above, so the last turn of a capped round is a named
    statement about the round instead of whatever payload the last tool
    happened to return, and `hop.partial` names that exit.
    """
    spent = it >= MAX_ITER
    win = leg_of(rows, "leg-window") or {"turns": []}
    mem = leg_of(rows, "leg-memory")
    # Every turn of the round is shown (GH #282): an `advice` turn has to read
    # as something said -- the agent has to see what the advisor came back
    # with, and the correlation id it carries is the reply half of the
    # bilateral lane -- and anything that is not the agent's own voice is the
    # other side of the conversation, SAYING WHICH OTHER SIDE IT IS (GH #540,
    # `wire_turn` above).
    #
    # A peer row of THIS turn that arrived without a speaker is named here, out
    # of the brief's `who` (GH #847) -- the fan-in is the first moment both are
    # known. The `collect` phase writes the same two fields onto the row, so a
    # deferred row reads them from the store and never from a later brief.
    #
    # A row a trusted gate named keeps its name: either field set is the
    # gate's word, and the brief fills only a row with neither (rev-T2 m-5).
    who = who_of(leg_of(rows, "leg-brief"))
    turns = []
    for t in win.get("turns", []):
        if (who and t.get("role") == "peer" and unnamed(t)
                and str(t.get("turn_id") or "") == turn_id):
            t = dict(t, speaker=who["name"], speaker_ref=who["ref"])
        turns.append(t)
    msgs = [wire_turn(t) for t in turns]
    thread, stale, names = thread_of(rows)
    msgs.extend(thread)
    sysm = system_of(mem)
    # THE AMBIENT BUNDLE, delivered as the evidence it is (GH #278): the last
    # two entries of the conversation are a `memory_recall` call and its result.
    # It used to enter as `system.memory` and STAY there -- durable state, in
    # the place an agent's instructions live, with nothing saying it was the
    # answer to one question asked once. A model reading a lookup presented as
    # configuration discounts it, and a slot nothing expires goes stale in
    # silence.
    if MEMORY_TIER and mem:
        call = recall_call(mem)
        msgs.append(call)
        msgs.append({"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                     "id": call["id"], "text": bundle_text(mem)})
    # THE BRIEF, delivered the same way and for the same reasons (GH #834): a
    # synthetic `affinity_brief` pair behind the memory pair, evidence of THIS
    # turn and never `system.*`. An empty leg -- no counterpart, the knob set
    # after the turn opened, an error -- renders nothing: a call whose result
    # says nothing is a question the model did not ask and cannot use.
    brief = leg_of(rows, "leg-brief")
    if isinstance(brief, dict) and str(brief.get("text") or ""):
        msgs.extend(brief_pair(brief))
    # The reply half of the bilateral lane (R-CG-3): a model can only pass a
    # correlation id back if it was shown one. The ids of the advice turns in
    # this round travel as data -- no prose, no rendering -- and so do the ids
    # an advisor answered under EARLIER in the session, for as long as their
    # departure stands (`held_of`, OR-KX-63): the question an advisor asks
    # back is answered by the person in a LATER round, which carries no advice
    # turn, and a model that no longer sees the id cannot pass it back. They
    # expire with the departure -- replaced by a newer one under the same id,
    # or past `DEPART_AFTER_MS` -- and only the youngest `HELD_CONSULTS` show.
    consults = [str(c) for c in (win.get("consults") or []) if str(c or "")]
    for t in win.get("turns", []):
        cid = str(t.get("consult_id", "") or "")
        if cid and cid not in consults:
            consults.append(cid)
    # The slot travels UNCONDITIONALLY (GH #259). `system.*` is durable state in
    # the brain cell: it is upserted per slot path, so a path that is not sent
    # is a path that is not TOUCHED. A slot that is only ever set therefore
    # keeps naming a consultation that closed long ago -- the promise above
    # ("they expire ... ") is kept by sending the empty rendering, not by
    # falling silent. Durable state is revoked, never merely abandoned.
    #
    # The system tree reaches a provider through `text` leaves only, so the ids
    # get one -- and the emptied slot needs it too: the leaf is what the upsert
    # overwrites, and `{"open": []}` alone would produce no leaf and no write.
    # Three words of label and the raw ids; the collector still renders nothing,
    # it just makes the data readable where it has to be read. The empty text
    # contributes nothing to the prompt, which is the intended "nothing open".
    sysm = dict(sysm)
    # WHICH JOB THIS ROUND IS, written on EVERY assembly and for the reason the
    # slot below it is written on every assembly (welle-live). In a duplex call
    # the brain advises a model that is already speaking; on every other turn it
    # answers, and the empty text says so. A slot that were only ever SET would
    # keep advising a brain for the rest of its life after one duplex call --
    # `system.*` is upserted per slot path in the brain cell, so a path that is
    # not sent is a path that is not touched. Durable state is revoked, never
    # merely abandoned.
    #
    # The family is `instructions`, one path beside the charter (`reply`, the
    # `in_pack` lane) and the block contract (`sidecar`, the menu lane), and no
    # `$replace` marker -- neither may revoke the other.
    #
    # `peer` is the second path of the family written here and for the same
    # reason (GH #847): the fixed rule that a peer turn is someone else's words,
    # set while a peer turn stands in the round -- or while the session's peer
    # mark stands among its departures (`held_of`, OR-KX-63): the curator keeps
    # showing an earlier peer turn in the window, and the rule that says what
    # it is has to stay beside it -- and EMPTY otherwise, so a brain that once
    # spoke with another colony is not told about strangers for the rest of
    # its life.
    peer_seen = (any(t.get("role") == "peer" for t in turns)
                 or bool(win.get("peer_held")))
    sysm["instructions"] = {
        "mode": {"text": MODE_ADVISE if engine == DUPLEX_ENGINE else ""},
        "peer": {"text": PEER_RULE if peer_seen else ""}}
    # THE LEGEND (GH #847, OR-SN-36): who the references in the frames are --
    # `<ref> = <name> (<identity>)`, one line per participant of the session,
    # in the order they joined. Out of the `roster` rows the turn opened with,
    # plus the counterpart this turn's brief named if it is not in them yet
    # (`collect` writes that row). One writer, every assembly; the text changes
    # on a join or a leave and on nothing else, which is what keeps the prompt
    # prefix of two turns byte-identical.
    #
    # EMPTY UNTIL THE OTHER SIDE HAS SPOKEN (OR-SN-72, rev-T2 I-3): the
    # counterpart joins only on a turn that carries a peer row. A channel that
    # names a counterpart but carries only the person's own words -- the
    # shipped assistant talkies brief on every turn -- has no stranger in it,
    # and a legend there would tell the model about one.
    joiner = who if (who and win.get("peer_turn")) else None
    sysm["roster"] = {"text": roster_text(roster_of(win.get("roster"), joiner))}
    sysm["consult"] = {"open": consults,
                       "text": ("open consults: " + ", ".join(consults)
                                + "\n" + CONSULT_RULE
                                if consults else "")}
    # THE BLOCK CONTRACT IS NOT WRITTEN HERE ANY MORE (GH #606). It used to be:
    # this cell held the memory hive's annotation as a literal and wrote it on
    # every assembly, which is what GH #525 needed to reach a brain whose birth
    # was behind it. The lesson survives the move -- a seed is written once, at
    # birth, so a grown brain never receives one -- and the slot that replaced it
    # is the SAME durability class as `system.tools`: derived from the offers,
    # written on the menu lane, re-derived on every mutation receipt this hive
    # hears. What moved is not the delivery, it is the OWNERSHIP of the words: a
    # contract this cell typed could describe exactly one consumer, and there
    # are two.
    #
    # Only on the spent branch (GH #570), and LAST: the promise the sentence
    # makes is that it is the last turn.
    if spent:
        msgs.append(partial_answer_turn(thread, names))
    out = {"header": head("answer" if spent else "curate", "", extra={
        "iter": str(nxt),
        "window_turns": str(len(win.get("turns", []))),
        # The marks of the caps and of the budget projection this cell no
        # longer has (GH #889) stay on every seam, zero: a CEL modifier that
        # reads a missing key FAILS, and a failed modifier skips the edge.
        "window_dropped": "0",
        "window_capped": "0",
        "round_dropped": "0",
        "round_capped": "1" if spent else "0",
        # PRESENT ON EVERY EMISSION, like every other key of this head. It
        # names the iteration cap and the partial answer that came with it
        # (GH #570).
        "partial": "1" if spent else "0",
        "round_stale": "1" if stale else "0",
        "round_deferred": "1" if win.get("deferred", 0) else "0",
        # The receipt of a scope that changed inside a session (GH #845,
        # R-SN-1): "1" on the first assembly of the turn that changed it, the
        # stderr line of the `turn-open` phase beside it. Present on every
        # seam, for the reason every key of this head is.
        "scope_changed": "1" if (win.get("scope_changed") and nxt == 0) else "0",
        "memory_capped": "0",
        "tokens_window": "0", "tokens_projected": "0", "tokens_estimated": "0",
        "curate_mark": "none", "curate_stage": "0", "curate_elided": "0",
        "curate_saved": "0", "curate_tools": "0", "curate_slots": "0"}),
        "messages": msgs}
    if sysm:
        out["system"] = sysm
    # THE CHANNEL'S SCOPE, on every `curate` of the session (GH #845): out of
    # the session row the round opened with, so a tool result, an advice and a
    # counselor's insertion carry it exactly like the turn that stated it. The
    # `llm` cell filters its menu for this one request; the menu in its store
    # stays whole. Absent when the session has none.
    scope = win.get("scope") if isinstance(win.get("scope"), dict) else {}
    if scope and not spent:
        out["tool_scope"] = scope
    return out


def drop_round(key):
    """The rows of a round, dropped when the round ends (OR-KX-V2): the curator
    keeps what was said, so this cell holds only what its fan-in still needs
    (R-27-1, GH #889). The `depart` rows stay: a late consult still looks its
    round up by them (GH #728), and an answered one stays open for the next
    round of its session (OR-KX-63). A round that never reaches here -- its
    brain call failed -- falls at a later turn-open once its last row is past
    `STALE_AFTER_MS` (OR-KX-68, `stale_of`)."""
    return cstore_bundle(
        [("c-drop-turns", {"operation": "delete", "table": "turns",
                           "where": {"session_id": session, "turn_id": key}}),
         ("c-drop-round", {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
                           "where": {"turn_id": key,
                                     "role": {"neq": "depart"}}})],
        "round-drop", key)


def seam_out(rows, nxt):
    """The seam plus its bookkeeping, in the same multi-send.

    Deferred turns (GH #103) that ride in this assembly are dropped -- their
    rows here and the legs their own opening parked -- rather than only
    unstamped: their words travel on `curate`, and the curator keeps them from
    here on (OR-KX-V2). A round that leaves on `answer` drops its own rows the
    same way (`drop_round`)."""
    msg = curate_message(rows, nxt)
    out = [msg]
    ridden = (leg_of(rows, "leg-window") or {}).get("deferred_turns") or []
    if msg["header"].get("round_deferred") == "1" and ridden:
        out.append(cstore_bundle(
            [("c-defer-turns", {"operation": "delete", "table": "turns",
                                "where": {"session_id": session,
                                          "turn_id": {"in": ridden}}}),
             ("c-defer-round", {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
                                "where": {"turn_id": {"in": ridden}}})],
            "defer-clear"))
    if msg["header"].get("route") == "answer":
        out.append(drop_round(turn_id))
    return out


# ==================================================================== LANES
# Lanes are read BEFORE phases: a message that arrives over a port edge carries
# whatever col_phase the chain happened to leave in its context, and the lane is
# the only thing that says what it IS.

# THE MENU IS ASKED FOR, NOT TYPED (GH #464). Two lanes and one round trip, and
# what comes back is DURABLE state of the agent. It travels its own lane, it
# lands in `system.*`, and the curator keeps it per slot path (`in_slots`) until
# something overwrites that exact path.
#
# WHY IT IS NOT A PER-TURN COST. The tools hive answers questions and raises
# nothing of its own, so somebody has to ask -- and asking in front of every
# assembly would buy a menu nobody typed at the price of a round trip per turn.
# The tick asks, the answer is written once, and every turn after it reads a slot
# that is already in the brain.
#
# WHY IT IS A TICK AND NOT A BIRTH. The substrate hands a cell no message at
# spawn, so the first ask is the first tick rather than the boot itself. That is
# the honest form, and it is also the useful one: a tool ADDED to the hive by
# mutation reaches this agent at the next tick, and nothing over there had to
# push -- which is exactly what the hive's own contract says about asking again.
if lane == "in_menu_tick":
    if not TOOLS_DECLARED:
        park()
    emit([{"header": head("schemas", "", "",
                          {"asked_count": str(len(TOOLS_DECLARED))}),
           "tools": list(TOOLS_DECLARED), "messages": []}])

if lane == "in_menu":
    schemas = [x for x in (d.get("schemas") or []) if isinstance(x, dict)]
    unknown = [str(n) for n in (d.get("unknown") or []) if isinstance(n, str)]
    menu = [provider_tool_of(x) for x in schemas if str(x.get("name") or "")]
    # THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME ANSWER (GH #606). `sidecar[]` travels beside
    # `schemas[]` on the same lane, from the same answerer, and is merged by the
    # same key -- because it is the same question read one word wider: what does
    # this agent get to ask its model for. A tool is one answer to it; a section
    # of the block the splitter cuts is the other.
    offers = sidecar_offers_of(d.get("sidecar"))
    if not menu and not offers:
        # An empty menu is never WRITTEN, and since GH #529 it is never
        # RECORDED either. `tools_slot` replaces the whole subtree, so a write
        # here would revoke the model's entire tool set on the strength of an
        # answer that found nothing -- and overwriting this answerer's stored
        # half with an empty one would do the same thing one tick later. The
        # other answerers' halves stand untouched.
        #
        # The question is asked of BOTH halves since GH #606, and only an answer
        # empty in both is parked. An answerer that offers a section without
        # declaring a tool -- a screen is the shipped case -- has answered, and
        # its row records an empty submenu because that is what it said. What the
        # guard still refuses is the write, and the merge below refuses it again
        # from the other side.
        sys.stderr.write("collector: the schemas answer carried no declaration"
                         " and no sidecar offer this collector could use%s\n"
                         % ((" -- nothing under: " + ", ".join(unknown))
                            if unknown else ""))
        park()
    # THE MENU IS A UNION, AND THE UNION NEEDS A MEMORY (GH #529). Before it,
    # one answer WAS the menu: parse, add the self-served names, write the lot
    # with `$replace`. That is right while exactly one thing answers and is the
    # whole defect the moment two do -- the second answer would not merge with
    # the first, it would delete it, and the two would take the menu away from
    # each other on every tick forever.
    #
    # So each answerer's last submenu is kept as one row of this hive's own
    # store, keyed by WHO delivered it, and the menu is re-derived from all the
    # rows on every answer. Delete-then-insert rather than an update, because
    # the store has no upsert and a first answer has no row to update; the
    # select rides in the same bundle, so it runs over the same connection
    # AFTER the write and sees it (GH #419). Two answerers replying at the same
    # time therefore converge: whichever bundle runs second sees both rows and
    # writes the full union.
    #
    # `unknown` travels with the row instead of being reported here: a name one
    # answerer has nothing under may be a name ANOTHER one delivers, and
    # reporting per answer would make every tick of a two-answerer tree warn
    # about the half of the menu it did not ask this answerer for.
    emit([cstore_bundle(
        [("c-menu-del", {"operation": "delete", "table": "menu",
                         "where": {"answerer": answerer}}),
         ("c-menu-put", {"operation": "insert", "table": "menu",
                         "row": {"answerer": answerer, "tools": menu,
                                 "sidecar": offers,
                                 "unknown": ",".join(unknown),
                                 "recorded_at": now}}),
         ("c-menu-all", {"operation": "select", "table": "menu",
                         "columns": ["answerer", "tools", "sidecar",
                                     "unknown"]})],
        "menu-merge")])
def open_round(tid, query, first, pair=None, more=()):
    """The turn-open bundle every round of this cell starts with, whatever
    opened it: `first` is the op that puts this round's row in place (a fresh
    insert, or the re-key of an advice row parked in the stage before), `pair`
    the answer half a duplex turn brings along. Then the open-round check, the
    session's turn rows, the session state -- and the memory leg beside the
    bundle.

    GH #419: the row, the open-round check and the read in ONE message. The
    row op is in FRONT of the read in the same bundle, so the read contains
    this very turn -- exactly as it did when the two were two messages, and for
    the same reason: a bundle's ops run in order over the store's one
    connection."""
    calls = [first] + (list(pair) if isinstance(pair, list)
                       else ([pair] if pair else [])) + list(more)
    # WHAT NOTHING ELSE ENDS FALLS FROM HERE (OR-KX-68), on every turn-open
    # and for every session. A DEPARTURE on its own clock, row by row -- each
    # is the bookkeeping of one call (`DEPART_AFTER_MS`: a consult nobody
    # answered or replaced, a quiet session's peer mark). A ROUND by the age
    # of its LAST row (review M-1): the two reads hand the reply every round
    # row but the departures and every turn row not deferred, and the reply
    # drops the rounds whose newest row is past `STALE_AFTER_MS` (`stale_of`)
    # -- the store has no aggregate, so that cut cannot be a `where`. A
    # deferred row waits for a round and leaves with it, so it is never read
    # here. In FRONT of the open-round check, which the reply reads without
    # the stale rounds: a round dead that long no longer holds a new turn
    # back; one merely idle (`round_idle_ms`) still gets the close of GH #103.
    calls.extend([
        ("c-open-stale-depart",
         {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
          "where": {"role": "depart", "recorded_at": {"lt": DEPART_CUT}}}),
        ("c-open-age-turns",
         {"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
          "columns": ["turn_id", "recorded_at"],
          "where": {"deferred": 0}}),
        ("c-open-age-round",
         {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
          "columns": ["turn_id", "recorded_at"],
          "where": {"role": {"neq": "depart"}}})])
    # THE PEER MARK (OR-KX-63): a turn that brings the other side's words
    # leaves one mark among the session's departures -- the older one replaced
    # -- so `instructions.peer` stays beside the peer turns the curator keeps
    # showing, after this round's rows are gone. The correlation is empty,
    # which no advice lookup ever asks for (`c-look-depart` needs an id).
    if PEER_SPOKE:
        calls.extend([
            ("c-open-peer-drop",
             {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
              "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "depart",
                        "correlation": ""}}),
            ("c-open-peer-mark",
             {"operation": "insert", "table": "round",
              "row": {"turn_id": tid, "session_id": session, "iter": 0,
                      "role": "depart", "turn": json.dumps({"peer": 1}),
                      "fired": 1, "recorded_at": now, "correlation": "",
                      "deadline_ms": 0}})])
    calls.extend([
             # Since GH #103 the chain first asks whether a tool round of the
             # session is still open -- an assistant row whose guard has not
             # fired -- because a mid-round turn defers instead of assembling.
             ("c-open-round",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
               "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "recorded_at", "session_id"],
               "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}),
             # The session's turn rows, read UNCONDITIONALLY. Only this
             # round's own and the deferred ones ride on `curate`
             # (`round_turns`); a row of an ended round is gone already
             # (OR-KX-V2), so the read stays small. A deferring turn throws it
             # away -- and buys the two messages the turn-open/win chain used
             # to cost. The decision stays in code, where it always was.
             ("c-open-win",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
               "columns": ["id", "session_id", "turn_id", "role", "content",
                           "recorded_at", "deferred", "consult_id", "speaker",
                           "speaker_ref"],
               "where": {"session_id": session},
               "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}]}),
             # The session's departures (OR-KX-63): the bookkeeping of calls
             # that left, which outlives the rounds they left from -- the ids
             # an advisor answered under, and the peer mark (`held_of`).
             ("c-open-depart",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
               "columns": ["correlation", "turn", "recorded_at"],
               "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "depart"},
               "order_by": [{"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "asc"}]})])
    # THE SESSION ROW (GH #845): the channel's tool scope, kept where every
    # round of the session reads it. Only an `in_turn` that STATES a scope
    # writes it -- the old row is read first, so the next phase can tell a
    # change from a first statement, then replaced (the store has no upsert:
    # delete-then-insert, the menu merge's form). Every opening, whatever its
    # lane, reads the row back, so an advice round carries the scope of the
    # session it answers without ever stating one.
    if SCOPE_STATED:
        calls.extend([
            ("c-open-scope-was",
             {"operation": "select", "table": "session",
              "columns": ["session_id", "tools_allow", "tools_deny"],
              "where": {"session_id": session}}),
            ("c-open-scope-del",
             {"operation": "delete", "table": "session",
              "where": {"session_id": session}}),
            ("c-open-scope-put",
             {"operation": "insert", "table": "session",
              "row": {"session_id": session, "tools_allow": SCOPE_ALLOW,
                      "tools_deny": SCOPE_DENY, "recorded_at": now}})])
    calls.append(
        ("c-open-scope",
         {"operation": "select", "table": "session",
          "columns": ["session_id", "tools_allow", "tools_deny"],
          "where": {"session_id": session}}))
    # THE LEGEND'S ROWS (GH #847, OR-SN-36), the same way: an application
    # gate's `roster_leave` and `roster_add`, on `in_turn` only, in front of
    # the read that hands every round of the session its legend. A leave is a
    # delete by reference, an add an insert -- and an add counts only BESIDE A
    # WRITTEN PEER ROW (`PEER_SPOKE`): the legend stays empty until the other
    # side has spoken in the session (OR-SN-72), whoever says who is there. The store has no
    # conditional insert, so a repeated add of a reference already there is
    # inserted and taken out again by the turn-open reply (`roster_dedupe`):
    # the table holds one row per reference, the earliest, and the legend does
    # not move when a gate stamps the same participant on every turn.
    if lane == "in_turn":
        for i, ref in enumerate(names_of(ctx.get("roster_leave"))):
            calls.append(("c-open-roster-leave-%d" % i,
                          {"operation": "delete", "table": "roster",
                           "where": {"session_id": session, "ref": ref}}))
        adds = roster_entries(ctx.get("roster_add")) if PEER_SPOKE else []
        for i, e in enumerate(adds):
            calls.append(("c-open-roster-add-%d" % i,
                          {"operation": "insert", "table": "roster",
                           "row": {"session_id": session, "ref": str(e.get("ref")),
                                   "name": plain(e.get("name"), 64),
                                   "identity": plain(e.get("identity"), 160),
                                   "joined_at": "%s#%03d" % (now, i)}}))
    calls.append(
        ("c-open-roster",
         {"operation": "select", "table": "roster",
          "columns": ["ref", "name", "identity", "joined_at"],
          "where": {"session_id": session},
          "order_by": [{"col": "joined_at", "dir": "asc"}]}))
    if BRIEF_SLOTS and not counterpart:
        # NO COUNTERPART, NO BRIEF -- AND NO WAIT (GH #834, OR-AG-10). The leg
        # is expected by configuration, so a turn that has nobody to be briefed
        # about parks it EMPTY here, in the same bundle as its own row: the
        # fan-in completes on the window alone, exactly as it did without the
        # knob. A fallback subject would be a brief about somebody else.
        calls.append(("c-open-brief",
                      {"operation": "insert", "table": "round",
                       "row": {"turn_id": tid, "session_id": session,
                               "iter": 0, "role": "leg-brief",
                               "turn": json.dumps({"id": "", "subject": "",
                                                   "slots": list(BRIEF_SLOTS),
                                                   "text": ""}),
                               "fired": 0, "recorded_at": now}}))
    out = [cstore_bundle(calls, "turn-open", tid)]
    if MEMORY_TIER:
        # Asked HERE, once per turn, because the collector is the place that
        # gathers what a round needs. The ambient ask carries no
        # call id and no window: it is the free floor under every turn, and the
        # model has not seen the turn yet when it leaves (GH #78).
        out.append(recall_ask(query, MEMORY_TIER, tid))
    if BRIEF_SLOTS and counterpart:
        # The brief, asked HERE and once per turn for the reason the recall
        # above is (GH #834): the collector gathers what a round needs, and
        # the counterpart is known before the model has seen the turn.
        out.append(brief_ask(tid, counterpart))
    return out


def open_turn_row(rid, tid, role, query, correlation):
    return ("c-open-turn",
            {"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
             "row": {"id": rid, "session_id": session,
                     "turn_id": tid, "role": role,
                     "content": query, "recorded_at": now, "deferred": 0,
                     "consult_id": correlation}})


if lane in ("in_turn", "in_advice", "in_delegation"):
    # ONE chain, three occasions. `in_advice` is the return lane of the advisor
    # split (R-CG-3): the advisor's result -- or the question it asks back --
    # arrives long after the turn that asked ended with its interim answer, so
    # it cannot re-enter that round. It is assembled like a TURN and opens a
    # fresh one, which is what makes the follow-up reach the channel in the
    # agent's own voice instead of as a raw advisor reply.
    if op is not None or phase in ("turn-open", "collect", "round-check",
                                   "advice-look"):
        park()
    advice = lane == "in_advice"
    # The third occasion (welle-live): the voice model hands the backend an
    # errand of its own accord while it keeps talking to the caller
    # (`session.delegation.created`, R-25-4). It is an EVENT in exactly the
    # sense `in_advice` is one -- it belongs to no round of ours, it opens a
    # fresh one, and it is not something anybody in this conversation said.
    delegation = lane == "in_delegation"
    event = advice or delegation
    # An event carries the role of ITS conversation, so its text is read
    # without one; the row keeps `advice` or `delegation` as its own role, which
    # is neither the user's word nor the agent's own.
    query = any_text(d) if event else (text_of(d, "user") or any_text(d))
    # One name for the row, one for the correlation. Both events carry the
    # correlation in the same column (`consult_id`) because both are the half of
    # a bilateral exchange that can be passed back -- the advisor's consult and
    # the model's delegation.
    role = "advice" if advice else ("delegation" if delegation else "user")
    correlation = consult if advice else (delegation_id if delegation else "")
    rid = now + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
    if advice and consult:
        # A LATE ANSWER NEVER INVENTS AN IDENTITY (GH #728, ruling 2026-09-22).
        # This round belongs to the member turn whose consult it answers, and
        # that turn is named on the `depart` row `in_calls` wrote when the
        # consult left -- found by the correlation the advisor answered under.
        # The advisor's own hop is still never adopted: its id is a round of
        # ANOTHER hive (#724, `an_advisors_return_never_adopts_the_id_on_its_hop`).
        #
        # Two stages, because the round's key needs the label and the text of
        # this arrival does not survive a store hop: stage A parks the advice
        # row under a provisional key and asks for the departure in the same
        # bundle; stage B (`advice-look`, below) re-keys the row and opens the
        # round exactly as every other turn opens one.
        prov = str(uuid.uuid4())
        emit([cstore_bundle(
            [("c-look-depart",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
               "columns": ["turn_id", "deadline_ms", "turn"],
               "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "depart",
                         "correlation": consult},
               "order_by": [{"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "desc"}],
               "limit": 1}),
             ("c-look-turn",
              {"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
               "row": {"id": rid, "session_id": session, "turn_id": prov,
                       "role": role, "content": query, "recorded_at": now,
                       "deferred": 0, "consult_id": correlation}}),
             ("c-look-self",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
               "columns": ["id", "content", "consult_id"],
               "where": {"turn_id": prov}})],
            "advice-look", prov)])
    if delegation:
        # The delegation's label comes off its HOP (GH #728, OR-T12): the voice
        # cell stamps the turn that was open when the model delegated
        # (`open_turn_id`) on the `delegation` emission, so there is nothing to
        # look up -- the departure of a delegation is the voice cell's, not
        # ours. The hop and never the context: a lane that re-enters this cell
        # may still carry the id of the round before this one there.
        label = disarm(hop.get("turn_id"))[:80]
        tid = event_key(label, now_ms() + LATE_AFTER_MS)
    elif advice:
        # An advice with no correlation at all (a replayed or hand-sent event):
        # nothing to look up, so it opens its round as it always did.
        tid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    else:
        # THE ROUND IS THE TURN (display-hive.md 2 / 8.2). The id a CHANNEL
        # assigned on acceptance wins, and uuid4 is only the fallback for an
        # ingress that has no channel in front of it. It used to be minted here
        # unconditionally, which renamed the turn in the middle of its own road:
        # measured 2026-09-18 on the live colonies, the answer reached apps/chat,
        # apps/ambient and apps/voice2vision under this uuid while the chat
        # window still carried the channel's, so 4.13 -- the chat closes when a
        # canvas window carries the turn_id of the last turn -- had two ids to
        # compare and never fired.
        #
        # Hop before context, because the hop is what the arriving turn says and
        # the context may still hold the id of the round BEFORE this one on a
        # lane that re-enters the collector.
        #
        # An adopted id is a FOREIGN string, and uuid4 used to make these
        # questions unaskable. Each is answered in the lines below, and none of
        # them with "no shipped channel does that":
        #   * `~` -- the separator of this cell's event key
        #     `<label>~<deadline>~<hex>` (GH #728). Replaced, not refused:
        #     refusing would drop 8.2 for exactly the channel that chose the
        #     wrong character, and a `~` left standing would let a channel's
        #     stamp read as a label nobody gave it.
        #   * length -- the id becomes a store key and a hop header. Capped.
        # What is NOT guarded here, because it cannot be from inside this cell:
        # the same id arriving twice. A repeat would meet the previous turn's
        # unfired `leg-window` guard row and consume its fan-in. Both shipped
        # channels mint per turn (`chat#<hex16>` random, `<session>#<seq>`
        # monotonic), so the question belongs to whoever writes the next channel.
        tid = disarm(hop.get("turn_id") or ctx.get("turn_id"))[:128]
        if not tid:
            tid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    # THE ANSWER HALF OF THE SAME TURN (R-25-9, welle-live). A duplex voice cell
    # cuts a turn on the MODEL's clock -- a user block plus the agent fragments
    # that follow it -- and therefore delivers both sides in ONE arrival: the
    # model decided by itself when it spoke, so there is no later `in_answer` to
    # write the other half. Both rows carry the same `turn_id`.
    #
    # The id is derived from the question's rather than drawn beside it: `id` IS
    # this table's time order, both rows are minted in the same microsecond, and
    # two random hex strings would put the answer in front of the question in
    # the round as often as behind it.
    #
    # Only on `in_turn`: an event has no second half, and an empty assistant
    # text is a turn nobody spoke.
    #
    # NEVER WITH A PEER TURN IN THE ARRIVAL (GH #847). A frame from another
    # colony is somebody else's conversation: an `assistant` turn in it is that
    # side's agent, not this one, and filing it as this agent's answer would
    # put words in its mouth that it never said (measured: F5, the pair row).
    if PEER_ARRIVAL:
        # EVERY peer turn is a row of its own, in arrival order, beside the
        # person's own words if the arrival carries any -- a room delivers
        # several speakers at once, and keeping only the last would drop the
        # others from the conversation. The ids are the first row's plus a
        # counter, so the store's id order IS the arrival order. What a
        # trusted gate set as speaker stays; what is missing is filled from
        # the brief at the fan-in (`curate_message`, `collect`).
        #
        # A peer turn of ANY type with text is a peer row (a `tool_call` of the
        # other side is still the other side's words); a peer turn without
        # text has nothing a row can hold and drops out. The person's
        # own turns keep the reading they always had: text turns only.
        rows_in = [m for m in (d.get("messages") or [])
                   if isinstance(m, dict) and str(m.get("text", "") or "")
                   and (m.get("origin") == "peer"
                        or (m.get("origin") == "user"
                            and m.get("type") in ("text", None)))]
        if not rows_in:
            # Nothing but textless peer turns: no row, no round, and never
            # the person's road below. Said, like every other refusal here.
            sys.stderr.write("collector: a peer turn without text for session"
                             " %s -- nothing to open\n" % session)
            # A gate's LEAVE still counts (rev-T2 fix round 1, m-1 a): a
            # participant leaving is exactly the event that may carry no
            # words, and parked here it would stay in the legend for good. A
            # scope statement is NOT taken here (OR-SN.T2.14): the scope is
            # for brain calls, this arrival makes none, and the channel edge
            # stamps it again on the next arrival that does.
            leaves = [("c-roster-leave-%d" % i,
                       {"operation": "delete", "table": "roster",
                        "where": {"session_id": session, "ref": ref}})
                      for i, ref in enumerate(names_of(ctx.get("roster_leave")))]
            if len(leaves) == 1:
                emit([store_op(leaves[0][1], "roster-leave", tid)])
            if leaves:
                emit([cstore_bundle(leaves, "roster-leave", tid)])
            park()
        ops = []
        for i, m in enumerate(rows_in):
            row = {"id": rid if i == 0 else "%s-%03d" % (rid, i),
                   "session_id": session, "turn_id": tid,
                   "role": "peer" if m.get("origin") == "peer" else "user",
                   "content": str(m.get("text")), "recorded_at": now,
                   "deferred": 0, "consult_id": ""}
            if row["role"] == "peer":
                row["speaker"] = plain(m.get("speaker"), 64)
                row["speaker_ref"] = (str(m.get("speaker_ref"))
                                      if ref_ok(m.get("speaker_ref")) else "")
            ops.append(("c-open-turn" if i == 0 else "c-open-turn-%d" % i,
                        {"operation": "insert", "table": "turns", "row": row}))
        query = str(rows_in[-1].get("text"))
        emit(open_round(tid, query, ops[0], ops[1:]))
    spoken = text_of(d, "assistant") if lane == "in_turn" else ""
    pair = None
    if spoken:
        pair = ("c-open-pair",
                {"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
                 "row": {"id": rid + "-a", "session_id": session,
                         "turn_id": tid, "role": "assistant",
                         "content": spoken, "recorded_at": now,
                         "deferred": 0, "consult_id": ""}})
    emit(open_round(tid, query, open_turn_row(rid, tid, role, query, correlation),
                    pair))

if lane == "in_bundle":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    # ONE port, ONE meaning since GH #552: the ambient leg of the turn. The
    # second meaning -- the answer to a `memory_recall` call, told apart by the
    # correlation key the request carried out -- moved into the memory hive,
    # which is where the call is answered now.
    emit([round_park("leg-memory", {"system": d.get("system", {}),
                                   "messages": d.get("messages", [])}, "collect", 0)])

if lane == "in_briefing":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    # The brief leg coming home (GH #834): affinity's answer -- or its error,
    # as an empty leg -- restamped onto this lane by the member's edge, under
    # the turn the member promoted from the request's hop (#535). Parked like
    # the memory leg; `collect` fires when every expected leg stands.
    emit([round_park("leg-brief", brief_leg(d), "collect", 0)])

if lane == "in_calls":
    if not turn_id:
        park_unkeyed("in_calls")
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    # The async class, as the dispatcher classified it (R-CG-3, delta 2). Those
    # ids are NOT part of the expectation set: they are acknowledged on the
    # spot, under their own tool_call_id, so the assistant turn stays
    # well-formed for every provider. And when nothing else was asked and the
    # turn is over anyway (see below), the row is filed as ALREADY fired -- no
    # guard to win, no open round for a sweep to find, and therefore no idle
    # window racing an advisor's thinking time.
    async_ids = [x for x in str(hop.get("async_calls", "") or "").split(",") if x]
    # The HANDOFF subset of the same classification (GH #372): the calls whose
    # lane also takes the TURN over. Declared at the dispatcher like the async
    # class itself and obeyed here -- which of the two a tool is, is tool
    # semantics, and this cell classifies nothing.
    handoff_ids = [x for x in str(hop.get("handoff_calls", "") or "").split(",") if x]
    ids = [str(m.get("id") or "") for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_call"]
    acked = [i for i in ids if i in async_ids]
    waiting = [i for i in ids if i not in async_ids]
    # WHAT ENDS A ROUND IS AN ANSWER (GH #372), and there are exactly two ways an
    # async-only bundle can have one. Filing the row as already fired ends the
    # round on the spot, which is honest only if this turn is going to be
    # answered by somebody:
    #
    #   * the model spoke beside the bundle -- the dispatcher already sent that
    #     sentence to the channel as the interim answer (it sends one only when
    #     there IS text, which is why this reads the turns the same way it does,
    #     one condition in two cells rather than two spellings of it); or
    #   * a HANDOFF call took the turn with it -- an advisor's event, an
    #     escalation re-entering the seam: the answer comes from a later turn.
    #
    # Neither, and the round is NOT over: the model has not answered yet. The
    # acknowledgements below complete the fan-in, the REGULAR guard fires, and
    # the seam re-enters the brain with everything the round collected. No new
    # route and no new sort -- the re-entry is bounded by params.max_iter like
    # every other round, and a spent budget leaves the same seam on 'answer'
    # with round_capped=1.
    #
    # Measured before the fix: a bare `remember` call -- fire-and-forget, async
    # but no handoff -- filed the round as fired and the channel got NOTHING. No
    # interim, no final, no error, and `round_idle_ms` does not fire on a quiet
    # channel. Three of five full harness runs died that way, and the per-turn
    # contract (GH #298) makes call-only iterations common.
    handed = [i for i in acked if i in handoff_ids]
    said = any(m.get("type") in ("text", None) and str(m.get("text", "") or "")
               for m in msgs)
    over = bool(said or handed)
    # THE DEPARTURE (GH #728). A handed call takes the turn's answer with it,
    # and what comes back later is an EVENT that opens a round of its own -- so
    # this is the last moment anybody knows which member turn it belongs to.
    # One `depart` row per handed call, in the SAME bundle as the assistant row:
    # the round key it left from, the correlation it will be answered under and
    # the deadline that later tells a leg from a straggler. `fired = 1` keeps it
    # out of every open-round question; the round readers (`round_sets`,
    # `thread_of`, the open-round check, the sweep) read `assistant`/`tool`
    # rows only, and the drop at the round's end leaves it standing.
    #
    # The correlation is the DISPATCHER's rule, `arguments.consult_id or call
    # id` (`async_keys`), and a lock runs both scripts over one response: a
    # fresh consult is named by its call, a reply to a question the advisor
    # asked back by the id it was shown -- which is the id the advisor answers
    # under, and the newest departure under it wins at the lookup.
    departs = []
    for m in msgs:
        cid = str(m.get("id") or "")
        if m.get("type") != "tool_call" or cid not in handed:
            continue
        try:
            fn = json.loads(m.get("text") or "{}")
        except Exception:
            fn = {}
        fn = fn if isinstance(fn, dict) else {}
        args = fn.get("arguments", {})
        if isinstance(args, str):
            try:
                args = json.loads(args or "{}")
            except Exception:
                args = {}
        args = args if isinstance(args, dict) else {}
        departs.append(("c-round-check-depart-%d" % len(departs),
                        {"operation": "insert", "table": "round",
                         "row": {"turn_id": turn_id, "session_id": session,
                                 "iter": it, "role": "depart",
                                 "turn": json.dumps({"id": cid,
                                                     "name": str(fn.get("name") or "")}),
                                 "fired": 1, "recorded_at": now,
                                 "correlation": str(args.get("consult_id") or cid),
                                 "deadline_ms": now_ms() + LATE_AFTER_MS}}))
    # A NEWER DEPARTURE ANSWERS THE OLDER ONE (OR-KX-68): the model passing an
    # id back IS the answer to the question the advisor asked under it, so the
    # older row of that id falls -- in the same bundle, in front of the new
    # one. What the lookup finds is unchanged (the newest row under the id);
    # there is simply one row left to find, and one id left to show.
    corrs = []
    for _cid, op in departs:
        c = op["row"]["correlation"]
        if c not in corrs:
            corrs.append(c)
    if corrs:
        departs.insert(0, ("c-round-check-depart-drop",
                           {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
                            "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "depart",
                                      "correlation": {"in": corrs}}}))
    ended = bool(acked and not waiting and over)
    out = [round_park("assistant", msgs, "round-check",
                      fired=1 if ended else 0,
                      more=departs)]
    out.extend(round_park("tool",
                          {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": i,
                           "text": "handed to the async lane: this answer"
                                   " arrives later as its own event"},
                          "round-check") for i in acked)
    if ended:
        # Filed as fired, the round is over on the spot -- and its rows go with
        # it, behind the acknowledgements (`drop_round`, OR-KX-V2).
        out.append(drop_round(turn_id))
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_tool":
    if not turn_id:
        park_unkeyed("in_tool")
    # WHAT A TOOL RESULT MAY CARRY (GH #252): its `messages[]` -- all of it, in
    # the order the tool wrote it -- and nothing else. Every turn is filed under
    # the `id` of the call it answers, because that correlation is the only one
    # a round has and the only one a provider has. This used to read `msgs[0]`,
    # so a tool that answered two calls in ONE message closed one of them and
    # left the other waiting for the idle sweep.
    #
    # The `system` slot of a tool result is deliberately NOT kept, and the
    # `in_bundle` lane above is not the precedent it looks like. `system.*` that
    # leaves this seam is UPSERTed into the brain cell's own cell.db and stays
    # there until something overwrites that exact slot path: it is DURABLE state
    # of the agent, not evidence of one round. A tool result gets no second
    # chance to correct itself, and a brief about one subject would still stand
    # in the prompt three subjects later. A tool with something to say says it
    # in the text of its result.
    #
    # RETRACTED with GH #278. This used to carve out one payload: the recall
    # bundle, it said, MAY live there because it is re-sent under a FIXED path
    # on every single turn and can therefore never go stale. It does not live
    # there any more. A durable slot is discounted by the model and goes stale
    # the first turn that does not re-send it. The bundle travels as the
    # `memory_recall` tool result of its own round now (`system_of`,
    # `recall_call`), which leaves the rule above without an exception.
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    # One turn stays a dict, which is the row shape every store already holds;
    # several travel as the list `thread_of` and `round_sets` both read.
    emit([round_park("tool", msgs[0] if len(msgs) == 1 else msgs, "round-check")])

if lane == "in_answer":
    if not turn_id:
        park_unkeyed("in_answer")
    # An interim answer is an answer -- it leaves on the same lane -- but it
    # says so, so a channel can render "one moment" differently from the real
    # reply (R-CG-3).
    is_interim = str(hop.get("interim", "")) == "1"
    mark = {"interim": "1"} if is_interim else {}
    # How the completion ended, carried onto the answer (GH #843): the brain's
    # hop names it, the splitter and the dispatcher pass it on, and a `length`
    # finish is marked as cut -- on the splitter road of talky and, since GH #892,
    # of cogny, and on the direct edge of a composite without a splitter alike,
    # which is why the mark is made here and not in the splitter.
    finish = str(hop.get("finish_reason", "") or "")
    mark["finish_reason"] = finish
    mark["truncated"] = "1" if finish == "length" else ""
    out = [{"header": head("answer", extra=mark), "messages": d.get("messages", [])}]
    if not is_interim:
        # The answer ends the round, and its rows go with it (`drop_round`).
        # An interim ends nothing: its calls are still out (R-CG-3).
        out.append(drop_round(turn_id))
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_round_sweep":
    # The re-check occasion a parent tree provides (GH #103): a timer or an
    # operator asks whether any round is stuck. The template never fires this
    # itself -- no schedule of its own, the session-keeper discipline. The
    # question is session-agnostic on purpose: a timer knows no session; the
    # rows carry theirs.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                    "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "session_id", "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}, "sweep")])

if lane in LANES:
    park()

# ==================================================== THE STORE SAID NO (#343)
# Since GH #331 every store error path stamps `hop.operation` with the refused
# op, so a refusal arrives looking exactly like an answer: the same phase in the
# context, the same op in the hop. Read as an answer it becomes `json.loads`
# over an error sentence, an empty row list, or -- worst -- a phase that
# advances on a read that never happened. `operation` says WHICH op answered,
# `error_code` says WHETHER it worked, and this cell reads both (the shape
# `builder-librarian/retrieve` was hardened into for GH #308).
#
# `op` is what says "this came from the store": nothing else that reaches this
# cell stamps it (the same discriminator the echo guards already use). So a hop
# carrying BOTH op and error_code is a store refusal, and a refusal is TERMINAL
# -- the chain stops here, no further store op leaves, and the failure is SAID.
#
# Measured before the fix: a refused window read wrote an EMPTY window leg into
# the round table, after which the turn fired and the model answered with no
# conversation at all -- and nobody learned. The report goes out where the turn
# was going anyway: on `answer`.
# GH #295: a BUNDLE reply never stamps `error_code` on the hop -- that header
# means "the whole reply is a refusal and carries no payload", and a bundle whose
# second leg failed still hands back the first leg's rows. It stamps
# `bundle_errors` instead, and here one refused leg is one too many: an assembly
# that fires on a half-read round is exactly the "answered with no conversation
# at all" failure #343 exists to prevent. WHICH leg failed is in `results[]`.
bundle_errors = int(hop.get("bundle_errors", 0) or 0)
if bundle_errors and not err:
    for _r in d.get("results") or []:
        if isinstance(_r, dict) and _r.get("error_code"):
            err = str(_r.get("error_code"))
            op = str(_r.get("operation") or op or "")
            break

if err and op and phase.startswith("menu"):
    # A menu is durable state and no turn travels beside it, so a store that
    # refuses one has nothing to report INTO the conversation: the `answer`
    # report below would put "context assembly stopped" in front of a person
    # who asked nothing. It is a warn line and a stop, and the next tick asks
    # again -- which is the whole reason the ask is a tick (GH #529).
    sys.stderr.write("collector: the menu merge stopped in phase '%s': the store"
                     " refused the %s with %s\n" % (phase, op, err))
    park()

if err and op:
    marks = {"store_error": err, "store_operation": str(op), "degraded": "1"}
    emit([{"header": head("answer", "", extra=marks),
           "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                         "text": "context assembly stopped in phase '%s': the store"
                                 " refused the %s with %s (%s)"
                                 % (phase, op, err, any_text(d))}]}])


# ================================================== THE MENU, MERGED (GH #529)
# Every answerer's last submenu, in one place, written with `$replace` exactly
# as one answer used to be. What is new is only WHOSE declarations the replaced
# subtree holds: all of them, plus the names this cell answers itself.
if phase == "menu-merge" and op == "bundle" and not err:
    rows = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-menu-all")
    menu, seen = [], set()
    # Deterministic by ANSWERER name, so the same rows produce the same menu in
    # the same order on every tick and a re-derivation is not a diff. A name two
    # answerers both declare is taken from the first of them: a menu that
    # declared one tool twice is a menu no provider accepts, and which of the
    # two won has to be decided by something a reader can predict.
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("answerer") or "")):
        tools = r.get("tools")
        if isinstance(tools, str):
            try:
                tools = json.loads(tools)
            except Exception:
                tools = []
        for t in (tools if isinstance(tools, list) else []):
            name = tool_name_of(t)
            if name and name not in seen:
                seen.add(name)
                menu.append(t)
    # THE SECTIONS, MERGED THE SAME WAY (GH #606). Same rows, same order, same
    # first-wins rule: two answerers offering one section name would produce a
    # block with one key described twice, and which of the two won has to be
    # something a reader can predict.
    sections, secs_seen = [], set()
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("answerer") or "")):
        offered = r.get("sidecar")
        if isinstance(offered, str):
            try:
                offered = json.loads(offered)
            except Exception:
                offered = []
        for o in sidecar_offers_of(offered):
            if o["section"] not in secs_seen:
                secs_seen.add(o["section"])
                sections.append(o)
    # A collector that does not ASK for the block ignores every offer of one,
    # silently: behind it stands no splitter (a composite without one -- `cogny`
    # until GH #892), so a section offered to it describes a fence nobody would
    # cut, and a warn line on every merge would report a correctly wired tree as
    # a defect.
    if not SIDECAR:
        sections = []
    if not menu and not sections:
        # The same guard as on the way in, on the other side of the round trip:
        # nothing recorded means nothing to write, and an empty `$replace` is a
        # revocation of the model's whole tool set.
        park()
    # UNKNOWN, against the MERGED menu (GH #529). A name is a finding only if
    # NOBODY delivered it -- not if the answerer that was asked had nothing
    # under it. That is what makes one declared list askable of several
    # answerers at once: the surface names `consult_cogny` beside its search
    # tools, the tool hive has nothing under the first and the core has nothing
    # under the other two, and neither of those is a defect.
    unknown = []
    for r in rows:
        for name in str(r.get("unknown") or "").split(","):
            name = name.strip()
            if name and name not in seen and name not in unknown:
                unknown.append(name)
    if unknown:
        # NAMED, never dropped. A name nobody has is a declaration in THIS
        # agent's template pointing at nothing, and the whole value of declaring
        # is that somebody can see the declaration was wrong. A `code` cell's
        # stderr lands in `log.jsonl` at warn level and stamps `had_stderr` on
        # the emission, so the line is a receipt a reader finds without opening
        # a body -- and `hop.menu_unknown` carries the same names on the
        # message itself.
        sys.stderr.write("collector: no answerer has a declaration for: %s\n"
                         % ", ".join(unknown))
    # THE BLOCK CONTRACT, COMPOSED (GH #606). It rides on the SAME message as
    # the menu because it is durable state of the same kind and derived from the
    # same rows: an `llm` cell upserts `system.*` per slot path, so this costs
    # one write per change and nothing per turn, and it is re-derived on every
    # mutation receipt this hive hears -- which is what reaches a brain whose
    # birth is behind it (the GH #525 lesson, kept).
    #
    # NOBODY OFFERING ANYTHING IS AN EMPTY SLOT, not a silence. Durable state is
    # revoked, never merely abandoned: a collector that fell silent here would
    # leave the last contract it wrote standing in a brain whose offers are gone,
    # and the model would keep fencing for a section nothing cuts any more. The
    # empty text contributes nothing to the prompt, which is the intended
    # "ask for no block at all" -- the pass-through the splitter behind it was
    # before the knob.
    sys_out = {}
    if menu:
        sys_out["tools"] = tools_slot(menu)
    written = []
    if SIDECAR:
        block, written = sidecar_block(sections) if sections else ("", [])
        sys_out["instructions"] = {"sidecar": {"text": block}}
    emit([{"header": head("menu", "", "",
                          {"menu_count": str(len(menu)),
                           # Empty since GH #889: this cell serves no tool of
                           # its own. Present, so no CEL guard fails on it.
                           "menu_self": "",
                           "menu_answerers": ",".join(
                               sorted(str(r.get("answerer") or "") for r in rows)),
                           "menu_unknown": ",".join(unknown),
                           "sidecar_sections": ",".join(written)}),
           "system": sys_out}])

# =================================================================== PHASES
# First assembly of a turn: window leg + optional memory leg, fanned in over
# the round table, fired exactly once by the guarded update. Since GH #103 the
# chain first asks whether a tool round of the session is still open -- an
# assistant row whose guard has not fired -- because a mid-round turn defers
# instead of assembling.
# GH #419: `turn-w`, `turn-open` and `win` were three messages for one question
# -- may this turn be assembled, and out of which rows. They are one now.

if phase == "advice-look" and op == "bundle":
    # Stage B of an advice (GH #728): the departure came back, or nothing did.
    # Found, the round is keyed on the member turn that sent the consult out,
    # with the deadline the departure stamped; a departure that itself left
    # from such a round passes ITS label on, so a consult answered inside an
    # advice round still names the member's turn. Not found -- a round from
    # before this build, a consult the dispatcher did not classify as a
    # handoff -- and the round keeps the provisional key: the behaviour before
    # the build, said once on stderr.
    mine = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-look-self")
    if not mine:
        # Nothing to re-key: the advice row stage A wrote under the provisional
        # key did not come back, and the advice ends here (T5 review M5 -- it
        # used to end without a sound).
        sys.stderr.write("collector: advice-look found no row under %s; the"
                         " advice is dropped\n" % turn_id)
        park()
    row = mine[0]
    rid = str(row.get("id") or "")
    query = str(row.get("content") or "")
    key = turn_id
    found = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-look-depart")
    answered = []
    if found:
        base = str(found[0].get("turn_id") or "")
        try:
            deadline = int(found[0].get("deadline_ms") or 0)
        except Exception:
            deadline = 0
        key = event_key(label_of(base) or base, deadline)
        # THE ADVISOR HAS ANSWERED UNDER THIS ID (OR-KX-63): the departure is
        # marked so, and its clock restarts. From here on every round of the
        # session shows the id in `system.consult` -- the advice round itself
        # and, above all, the person's next round, in which a question the
        # advisor asked back gets its answer. Until an advisor has answered,
        # there is nothing to reply to, so an unanswered departure shows
        # nothing (the reading of `collector@4.4.1`: ids of advice turns only).
        try:
            body = json.loads(found[0].get("turn") or "{}")
        except Exception:
            body = {}
        body = dict(body) if isinstance(body, dict) else {}
        body["answered"] = 1
        answered.append(("c-open-answered",
                         {"operation": "update", "table": "round",
                          "set": {"turn": json.dumps(body), "recorded_at": now},
                          "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "depart",
                                    "turn_id": base,
                                    "correlation": str(row.get("consult_id")
                                                       or consult)}}))
    else:
        sys.stderr.write("collector: no departure found for consult %s; the"
                         " advice round keeps an id of its own\n"
                         % str(row.get("consult_id") or consult))
    emit(open_round(key, query,
                    ("c-open-rekey",
                     {"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                      "set": {"turn_id": key}, "where": {"id": rid}}),
                    more=answered))

def session_of(doc):
    """What the session rows of a turn-open reply say (GH #845, #847): the
    channel's tool scope, whether this turn CHANGED it, and the legend rows.

    A change is a scope this turn stated that differs from the one the session
    row held before it. It is taken over -- the channel is the authority on its
    own scope, and a deploy that changes a channel's tools is expected to cost
    the prompt cache once (R-SN-1) -- and it is SAID: a stderr line here and
    `hop.scope_changed` on the turn's first assembly. A repeat is not a change.

    A FIRST statement is a change when the session was already running: no
    session row, but another turn's row still held here -- a channel that
    gained a scope by a deploy, a session begun before the collector kept
    scopes. The
    prompt cache breaks there all the same, so it is said all the same, as
    `none -> <new>` (rev-T2 I-2, R-SN-1). A first statement in a fresh session
    is the session's scope from its first word and changes nothing."""
    legs = results_by_id(doc)
    scope = scope_row(bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-scope"))
    changed = False
    if "c-open-scope-was" in legs:
        was_rows = bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-scope-was")
        was = scope_row(was_rows)
        # A row of a stale round is not a running session's (`stale_of`).
        stale = stale_of(doc)
        running = bool(was_rows) or any(
            str(r.get("turn_id") or "") not in [turn_id] + stale
            for r in bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-win") if isinstance(r, dict))
        if running and was != scope:
            changed = True
            sys.stderr.write(
                "collector: tool scope of session %s changed (%s -> %s)\n"
                % (session, json.dumps(was, sort_keys=True) if was else "none",
                   json.dumps(scope, sort_keys=True) if scope else "none"))
    return scope, changed, roster_of(bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-roster"))


def stale_of(doc):
    """The rounds dead past `STALE_AFTER_MS` (OR-KX-68), sorted: a round is as
    old as its LAST row, in the round table or among the turn rows under its
    key (review M-1) -- a round still at work keeps its early rows however long
    it runs. An undatable row dates nothing; the turn being opened is never
    stale."""
    newest = {}
    for cid in ("c-open-age-round", "c-open-age-turns"):
        for r in bundle_rows_of(doc, cid):
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            tid = str(r.get("turn_id") or "")
            at = str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
            if tid and at > newest.get(tid, ""):
                newest[tid] = at
    return sorted(t for t, at in newest.items()
                  if at < STALE_CUT and t != turn_id)


def stale_drop(stale):
    """The rows of the stale rounds (`stale_of`), dropped on the turn-open
    reply: their round rows and their turn rows, never a departure (its own
    clock) and never a deferred row (it leaves with the round it rides)."""
    return cstore_bundle(
        [("c-stale-turns", {"operation": "delete", "table": "turns",
                            "where": {"turn_id": {"in": stale}, "deferred": 0}}),
         ("c-stale-round", {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
                            "where": {"turn_id": {"in": stale},
                                      "role": {"neq": "depart"}}})],
        "stale-drop")


def held_of(doc):
    """What the session's departures hold past the round (OR-KX-63): the
    youngest `HELD_CONSULTS` ids an advisor has answered under, oldest first,
    and whether the peer mark stands. An unanswered departure holds nothing to
    show -- there is no question yet."""
    consults, peer = [], False
    for r in bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-depart"):
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        body = r.get("turn")
        if isinstance(body, str):
            try:
                body = json.loads(body or "{}")
            except Exception:
                body = {}
        body = body if isinstance(body, dict) else {}
        if body.get("peer"):
            peer = True
            continue
        cid = str(r.get("correlation") or "")
        if cid and body.get("answered"):
            if cid in consults:
                consults.remove(cid)
            consults.append(cid)
    return consults[-HELD_CONSULTS:], peer


def window_leg(doc):
    """The window leg of a turn: its turns (`round_turns`), with the session's
    state riding in it. The round's own rows are what every later assembly of
    the round reads, so the scope and the legend reach a tool round's re-entry
    without a store read and without a context key a round trip could lose."""
    raw = bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-win")
    win = round_turns(raw)
    scope, changed, roster = session_of(doc)
    if scope:
        win["scope"] = scope
    if changed:
        win["scope_changed"] = 1
    if roster:
        win["roster"] = roster
    consults, peer_held = held_of(doc)
    if consults:
        win["consults"] = consults
    if peer_held:
        win["peer_held"] = 1
    # Whether THIS turn brought a peer row (OR-SN-72): the one occasion on
    # which the brief's counterpart joins the legend. Read off the store's
    # rows.
    if any(isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("role") == "peer"
           and str(r.get("turn_id") or "") == turn_id for r in raw):
        win["peer_turn"] = 1
    return win


def roster_dedupe(doc):
    """One row per reference (rev-T2 m-3): every younger row of a reference the
    legend already holds is deleted, by its own `joined_at`. The store has no
    conditional insert, so a gate that stamps `roster_add` on every turn inserts
    a row each time; this takes it out again on the same reply. The legend text
    is unaffected either way -- `roster_of` lets the earliest row win."""
    first, out = {}, []
    rows = [r for r in bundle_rows_of(doc, "c-open-roster") if isinstance(r, dict)]
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (str(r.get("joined_at") or ""), str(r.get("ref") or "")))
    for r in rows:
        ref = str(r.get("ref") or "")
        if ref not in first:
            first[ref] = r
            continue
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "delete", "table": "roster",
                             "where": {"session_id": session, "ref": ref,
                                       "joined_at": str(r.get("joined_at") or "")}},
                            "roster-dedupe"))
    return out


if phase == "turn-open" and op == "bundle":
    out = []
    # The legend's younger duplicates, on the same reply and whatever the round
    # check decides -- a deferred turn's repeated add is taken out as well.
    out.extend(roster_dedupe(d))
    # The rounds dead past the frist (OR-KX-68, `stale_of`), dropped on the
    # same reply whatever the round check decides -- and left out of it.
    stale = stale_of(d)
    if stale:
        out.append(stale_drop(stale))
    # Open rounds the policy can date. An undatable open row predates #103 and
    # must neither be closed nor block the session forever: such a session
    # keeps the pre-#103 behaviour and assembles normally.
    open_rounds = [r for r in bundle_rows_of(d, "c-open-round")
                   if str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
                   and str(r.get("turn_id") or "") not in stale]
    if not open_rounds or not DEFER_TURNS:
        # No deferral (`defer_turns` "0", GH #894): the turn opens its own round
        # beside the open one, and an idle open round still gets its re-check
        # from this arrival, as it would below.
        emit(out + [round_park("leg-window", window_leg(d), "collect", 0)]
             + [re_check(r) for r in open_rounds
                if str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT])
    # A deferred turn still SAYS a changed scope (the stderr line, out of
    # `session_of` inside `window_leg`); the round it rides with reads the new
    # row when it next opens.
    held = window_leg(d)
    # Mid-round user turn (GH #103): the turn is written already and stays,
    # but it starts NO second assembly while a round of the session is open --
    # at most ONE open brain call per session, the telephone model (R-OS-3):
    # you answer when the sentence is finished. The stamp is what the next
    # regular assembly reports as round_deferred=1.
    #
    # EVERY row of a deferred turn is a deferred row -- the person's words, a
    # peer's, an advice, a delegation, the answer half of a duplex pair: with no
    # window behind this cell the stamp is the only way the next round finds
    # them (GH #889). The PEER rows are named by the turn's OWN brief, not by a
    # later one -- in a room the next turn may brief another counterpart. So a
    # deferred turn with a peer row parks a HELD window leg: its fan-in
    # completes on its own brief, writes the speaker and the join, and fires
    # nothing (`collect`).
    out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                         "set": {"deferred": 1},
                         "where": {"turn_id": turn_id}},
                        "defer-w", extra={"round_deferred": "1"}))
    if held.get("peer_turn"):
        out.append(round_park("leg-window",
                              {"held": 1, "peer_turn": 1, "turns": [],
                               "roster": held.get("roster") or []},
                              "collect", 0))
    for r in open_rounds:
        if str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT:
            # The parked arrival is itself the next OCCASION: a round whose
            # start lies behind the idle window gets its re-check, and the
            # regular round-check decides on full progress (GH #103).
            out.append(re_check(r))
    emit(out)

def speaker_ops(rows):
    """What the fan-in writes back once the brief has named the counterpart
    (GH #847), in the same multi-send as the seam: the speaker onto THIS turn's
    peer rows that arrived without one -- a row a trusted gate named keeps its
    name, the guard says so -- and the counterpart into the legend when the
    session's legend does not hold its reference yet. Nothing without a `who`."""
    who = who_of(leg_of(rows, "leg-brief"))
    win = leg_of(rows, "leg-window") or {}
    # Nothing without a `who`, and nothing on a turn without a peer row: the
    # counterpart joins the legend with the other side's first words
    # (OR-SN-72), and there is no peer row to name either.
    if not who or not win.get("peer_turn"):
        return []
    # Only a row with NEITHER field is named (rev-T2 m-5, `unnamed`).
    out = [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                     "set": {"speaker": who["name"], "speaker_ref": who["ref"]},
                     "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "role": "peer",
                               "speaker_ref": {"or_null": {"eq": ""}},
                               "speaker": {"or_null": {"eq": ""}}}},
                    "speaker-w")]
    known = {r.get("ref") for r in roster_of(win.get("roster"))}
    if who["ref"] not in known:
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "roster",
                             "row": {"session_id": session, "ref": who["ref"],
                                     "name": who["name"],
                                     "identity": who["identity"],
                                     "joined_at": now}}, "roster-w"))
    return out


if phase == "collect" and op == "bundle":
    # GH #419 -- the election, without the guard. The window leg parks and the
    # round table is read back in the SAME message: the store runs a bundle's ops
    # in order over its one connection, so the trailing select sees the insert in
    # front of it and of two legs parking concurrently exactly ONE reads a
    # complete set. That is what `gate` (a select), `fire-guard` (a guarded
    # update) and `fire` (a second select) cost, three messages, for a decision a
    # bundle makes for free.
