    rows = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-collect-read")
    roles = {r.get("role") for r in rows}
    if not set(EXPECT) <= roles:
        park()
    if len([r for r in rows if r.get("role") == "leg-window"]) > 1:
        # A redelivered leg is a duplicate, not a complete set: firing on it
        # would assemble the same turn twice.
        sys.stderr.write("collector: the window leg parked twice for %s\n" % turn_id)
        park()
    # The `fired` mark of the window leg, and it is the HALF of the old guard
    # that had to stay. `update ... where fired=0` did two jobs: it elected among
    # the legs racing to complete the round (the read-back does that now, for
    # free), and it made the election permanent -- a leg that lands AFTER the
    # turn has left reads a complete set too, and would assemble it a second
    # time. Only the first job went with GH #419.
    if any(int(r.get("fired") or 0) for r in rows if r.get("role") == "leg-window"):
        park()
    done = store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "round", "set": {"fired": 1},
                     "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "role": "leg-window", "fired": 0}},
                    "collect-done")
    if (leg_of(rows, "leg-window") or {}).get("held"):
        # A DEFERRED turn's fan-in (see `turn-open`): its speaker and its join,
        # and no seam -- the open round is the session's one brain call, and
        # the next regular assembly carries this turn's rows.
        emit([done] + speaker_ops(rows))
    emit(seam_out(rows, 0) + [done] + speaker_ops(rows))

# Tool round: the fan-in of the store-backed tool loop, now re-entering through
# the same seam and therefore carrying the round's opening and the bundle with
# it.
if phase in ("round-done", "collect-done") and op == "update":
    # The echo of the closing mark. Nothing follows it -- the seam left with it,
    # in the same multi-send -- and a chain that read this as an occasion would
    # assemble the turn a second time.
    park()

if phase == "sweep" and op == "select" and not err:
    # One re-check per stale open round, all rounds in parallel. Fresh rounds
    # wait, undatable rows keep their pre-#103 behaviour. A sweep that finds
    # nothing stale emits nothing: its observable effect is the round it
    # fires -- this lane is an occasion, not a report lane.
    emit([re_check(r) for r in rows_of(d)
          if str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
          and str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT])

if phase == "round-check" and op in ("bundle", "select"):
    # `re_check` (GH #103) asks the same question with a bare select: it names a
    # round worth looking at and parks nothing of its own. A bundle is TWO OR
    # MORE tool_calls (store `tool_call_turn_count`), so the two shapes are told
    # apart by the op and read out of the place each one puts its rows.
    # The same cure for the tool round (GH #419): a result parks and reads the
    # slate back in ONE message. `round_sets`, the idle exit and the IDLE_CUT
    # comparison are word for word what `round-check` ran -- only the row source
    # and the election changed.
    rows = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-round-check-read") if op == "bundle" else rows_of(d)
    # Same argument as at the assembly: the mark makes the election permanent.
    # A tool result that arrives after its iteration has fired -- the advisor's
    # late event is the ordinary case -- reads a complete set too, and without
    # this it would send the turn to the brain a second time.
    if any(int(r.get("fired") or 0) for r in rows
           if r.get("role") == "assistant" and int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0) == it):
        park()
    expected, received, progress = round_sets(rows, it)
    missing = expected - received
    if expected and not missing:
        # The `fired` mark stays, and it is NOT the guard it used to be. It says
        # the round is CLOSED (GH #103): `turn-open` reads it to decide whether a
        # mid-round turn defers, and the idle sweep reads it to decide what is
        # still worth re-checking. Both would otherwise keep finding a round that
        # has long since answered. What went with GH #419 is only its
        # `rows_affected` -- the election is the read-back above, and the mark
        # therefore travels WITH the seam instead of one hop in front of it.
        emit(seam_out(rows, it + 1)
             + [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "round",
                          "set": {"fired": 1},
                          "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "iter": it,
                                    "role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}, "round-done")])
    if expected and missing and progress and progress < IDLE_CUT:
        # The deterministic exit of GH #103: the round went idle with calls
        # still open, and a message reached this cell anyway. The stand-ins
        # complete the fan-in; everything after this is the regular machine.
        emit(lost_results(missing))
    park()

park()

max_iter.description: How many times a turn may re-enter the brain with a tool round. At the cap the seam leaves through the answer lane with hop.round_capped=1 instead of asking again - the seam opened the round, so the seam closes it.

round_idle_ms.description: Idle window of one tool round in milliseconds (default two minutes). A round whose last progress - the newest recorded_at of its rows - lies behind this window while its fan-in is still incomplete is closed at the NEXT message that reaches the cell anyway (the next result, the next turn, an in_round_sweep request): the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results with their tool_call_id kept, then the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. Pure arithmetic, no timer of the template's own.

late_after_ms.description: Deadline of a consult or a delegation in milliseconds (default 30 s, GH #728). A handed-over call leaves a `depart` row stamped now + this value; the answer of the round its return opens carries the member turn it belongs to as hop.turn_id and hop.late = "1" once the deadline has passed at the moment the answer leaves, "0" before. A straggler is never re-identified: each consumer treats it after its kind (a voice call after a turn change drops it, the chat delivers it). Set per assistant on the talky ref markers.

defer_turns.description: GH #894 (OR-KY-75): "1" (shipped) defers a turn that arrives while a tool round of its session is open to the next round the session opens (GH #103, one open brain call per session, the telephone model of a channel voice); "0" opens a round of its own for every turn, which a core sets, because a core's session is the conversation that consults it and a deferred errand or reply waited for a round nobody opened and came back under another errand's consult_id. Blank is the shipped value.

memory_tier.description: Memory leg. Empty = no memory leg: the recall port is not wired and the assembly waits for the window leg alone. '0' / '1' / '2' request that recall tier once per turn. What comes back reaches the brain as the result of a synthetic `memory_recall` call at the end of the round, never as durable system state (GH #278); system.memory carries the revocation of that slot and nothing else. This is the AMBIENT leg and the only one this cell has since GH #552: the deliberate `memory_recall` call a model makes is declared and answered by the member's memory hive.

memory_form.description: Which form of the bundle reaches the brain in the synthetic `memory_recall` tool result of the AMBIENT leg: 'readable' the rendered block a model reads, 'json' the machine-readable bundle, 'both' the two joined by a newline. The collector renders nothing of its own; both forms come from the memory hive verbatim. Since GH #552 it governs that leg ALONE -- the deliberate tool call is rendered by `memory-hive/tool`, which has a `form` of its own, because the two legs are two roads through two templates.

brief_slots.description: Slots to brief affinity about the counterpart of a turn; empty = no brief leg (GH #834). With slots set (`["peer", "channel"]` is affinity's vocabulary), a turn whose context carries `counterpart` -- an entity reference the entry edge of a channel with many counterparts stamps -- raises ONE `brief` at its opening, beside the memory leg, and the fan-in waits for its answer on `in_briefing`: the brief reaches the brain as a synthetic `affinity_brief` tool pair, never as `system.*`. A turn without `counterpart` asks nothing and parks the leg empty, so it waits for nothing (there is no fallback subject). An `error` answer is an empty leg. A comma string is read the same way as an array. The leg has no deadline: like the memory leg it is a synchronous leg of the turn's opening, so a knob set on a collector whose `brief` lane nobody wired leaves every turn with a counterpart waiting -- set it where the member's brief road is drawn (the assistant's two surfaces).

sidecar.description: The sidecar block contract (GH #606, GH #525). Non-empty composes the sections OFFERED on the menu lane into one block contract and writes it to system.instructions.sidecar beside system.tools -- a composed preamble (under 500 characters for the shipped pair: one fenced ```sidecar block after the answer, ONE JSON object, one top-level key per section, then the whole-object shape of this composition and the obligation with the section names in it), then one `## <section> (required|optional)` per offer with its instruction and a compact example rendered from its schema. Empty writes nothing at all. Ships OFF because what cuts the block back out of the answer is a splitter between brain and dispatcher and this cell cannot see whether one stands behind it: talky switches it on, and so does cogny since GH #892, which grew the talky's splitter; a composite without one leaves it off. Nobody offering anything is an EMPTY slot, not a silence -- durable state is revoked, never abandoned. The write carries no $replace marker, so the charter in instructions.reply is not touched, and the leaf name sorts after it on purpose.

sidecar_max_chars.description: The ceiling of the composed sidecar contract, in characters (GH #606). Over it, OPTIONAL sections fall from the back of the alphabetical order with a warn line naming what fell; a REQUIRED section never falls, because a section every turn has to carry is not a budget item -- a contract over the ceiling with only required sections left is kept and reported instead. Every character in here is re-read by the provider on every turn of every conversation.

tools.description: The tool names this agent DECLARES it uses (GH #464). At every tick of the menu lane the collector asks the tools hive for exactly these names and turns the answer into `system.tools` on route `menu` -- one durable write, not a per-turn cost. `["*"]` asks for everything the hive has. A comma string is read the same way as an array. Empty (the shipped default) asks for nothing at all. A name the hive does not have comes back in `hop.menu_unknown` and as a warn line in `log.jsonl` -- never as a silence.

messages.description: The turns of what leaves. OPTIONAL since 1.4.0: the `menu` route carries `system.*` and nothing else. Every other route still writes turns.

tools.description: The names this agent declares it uses, on the `schemas` route and nowhere else (GH #464). It is the whole body of the request: the tools hive keeps no table of who asks, so the caller says what it wants every time.

tool_scope.description: GH #845: the channel's tool scope, on the `curate` route and nowhere else -- `{"allow": [...], "deny": [...]}`, only the halves that name something, absent when the session has none. Out of the session row the round opened with, so every `curate` of the session carries it (a tool-result re-entry, an advice round, an insertion); the `llm` cell filters its menu for that one request and the menu in its store stays whole.

degraded.description: GH #343: "1" on a report the collector emits because it could NOT do what the lane asked -- today only when the store refused a read or a write. A parent that wants to render a failure differently from an answer branches on this key instead of parsing the text.

store_error.description: GH #343: the store's own `error_code` on a reply this lane refused to read as rows (`invalid_input`, `query_timeout`, `write_denied`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_column`, `constraint_violation`, `sql_error`, ...). Present exactly when `degraded` is.

store_operation.description: GH #343: the op the store refused, as `hop.operation` named it -- `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked.

curate_tools.description: Always "0" since GH #889: the curator owns the window. Present, so a CEL guard never fails on a missing key.

curate_slots.description: Always "0" since GH #889: the curator owns the window. Present, so a CEL guard never fails on a missing key.

asked_count.description: How many names one `schemas` request carried (GH #464).

menu_count.description: How many declarations the `menu` route wrote into `system.tools` (GH #464).

menu_self.description: Always empty since GH #889: this cell serves no tool of its own. Present, so a CEL guard never fails on a missing key.

menu_answerers.description: WHO the menu was merged from, comma-joined and sorted (GH #529): one name per answerer this cell holds a submenu for. The menu is a union over answerers since 3.4.0 -- a tool the composite reaches by an edge on its NAME is topology of the level that draws the edge, so the side that ANSWERS it is the side that declares it -- and this key is the receipt that says which of them the write actually stands on. Empty rather than absent, for the same reason as `menu_unknown` two keys down.

menu_unknown.description: The declared names NO answerer has anything under, comma-joined (GH #464, recomputed against the merged menu since GH #529). Before 3.4.0 this was per ANSWER, which made every tick of a two-answerer tree report the half of the list it had not asked that answerer for; a name is a finding only when nobody delivered it. Empty rather than absent, so an edge's CEL guard never fails on a missing hop key.

sidecar_sections.description: The sections that went into the composed block contract, comma-joined (GH #606): the union over every answerer's `sidecar[]`, required first and alphabetical inside each half, in the order the block states them -- so AFTER the `sidecar_max_chars` cap, not the offers the merge started from. Empty rather than absent, and empty means no section entered the contract: either nobody offered one (the slot is then written EMPTY, revoking the brain's last contract) or this collector does not ask for a block at all (`sidecar` off, and then nothing is written). `menu_answerers` beside it says who was asked.

round_id.description: On `answer`: the key of the round the answer left (GH #728). Equal to turn_id for an ordinary turn; for an advice or a delegation round it is the round's own key, and turn_id is the member turn it answers.

late.description: On `answer`: "1" when the round answers a consult or delegation whose deadline (late_after_ms) had passed when the answer left, "0" inside it, empty for every other answer (GH #728).

finish_reason.description: On `answer`: how the completion behind it ended, as the brain's hop named it -- `stop`, `length` -- and empty where this cell knows no reason (a spent round's digest, a store report, an interim sentence). Present on every answer since 2.3.0 (GH #843).

truncated.description: On `answer`: "1" when the completion was cut on `length`, empty otherwise -- present, never absent (GH #843). A consumer that must not pass on a half sentence refuses or marks it here.

scope_changed.description: GH #845: "1" on the first assembly of a turn whose channel stated a tool scope that differs from the one the session row held -- the new scope is taken over, and a stderr line names old and new. "0" on every other seam; present always, so a CEL guard never fails on a missing key.

messages.description: The turns of whatever arrived. OPTIONAL since 1.4.0: a lane may carry no turn (`in_menu` carries declarations); a body without turns simply carries no text, which the script already reads as the empty string.

system.description: The memory bundle's own subtree on `in_bundle`. Consumed on that lane and dropped on every other (GH #252).

schemas.description: The declarations the tools hive answered with, on the `in_menu` lane: one `{name, description, parameters}` per name it has (GH #464). Provider-neutral -- this cell wraps them.

unknown.description: The declared names the tools hive has nothing under, verbatim (GH #464). Reported, never dropped.

sidecar.description: The sidecar OFFERS of one menu answer (`in_menu`, GH #606): `{section, required, schema, instruction}` per section the answerer wants in the block the splitter cuts. Merged over answerers by section name exactly as `schemas[]` is merged by tool name, first answerer wins, and composed into `system.instructions.sidecar` under the `sidecar` knob.

who.description: GH #847: on `in_briefing`, affinity's `who {ref, name, identity, known}` beside the brief's text. Parked with the text as round state, never as `system.*`: it names the speaker of this turn's unnamed peer rows and, on a turn that carries a peer row, joins the legend `system.roster`. An error leg carries none.

sidecar_raw.description: GH #871, on `in_answer` only: the block a splitter cut out of the answer. Accepted and not kept since GH #889 -- the curator keeps the raw answer.

tool_answerer.description: WHO answered a `in_schemas` question (GH #529) -- the mirror of the `context.tool_caller` the request carries. It keys the submenu row this cell stores, so several answerers' declarations are merged instead of replacing each other. Absent is the one-answerer shape every tree had before 3.4.0 and counts as the default answerer, so nothing wired earlier changes behaviour.

counterpart.description: GH #834: the entity reference (`peer:<...>`) of the counterpart this turn is with, stamped by the entry edge of a channel with many counterparts beside `channel`. The subject of the brief leg and nothing else; absent or empty, no brief leaves and the leg is parked empty.

channel_node.description: GH #834: the surface the turn came in on (GH #522); the `channel` of a brief request, before `context.channel`.

channel.description: GH #834: the chat the turn is in; the `channel` of a brief request when no `channel_node` is set.

tools_allow.description: GH #845: the tool names the CHANNEL allows its sessions (an array, the same array as a JSON string, or a comma string), stamped by the channel edge and constant per session. Read on `in_turn` only and kept in the session row; never on `in_advice` or `in_delegation`.

tools_deny.description: GH #845: the tool names the CHANNEL takes away from its sessions; the same form and the same rule as `tools_allow`.

roster_add.description: GH #847: participants an application gate names as joining the channel, `[{ref, name, identity}]` (or the same list as a JSON string). Read on `in_turn` only and only beside a peer turn of the same arrival (the legend stays empty until the other side has spoken); a reference already in the legend changes nothing, and a repeated add is deleted again.

roster_leave.description: GH #847: the reference (or several) of a participant leaving the channel; its legend row is deleted. Read on `in_turn` only.

brief_outcome.description: GH #834: on `in_briefing`, the route affinity answered the brief with (`answer` or `error`), stamped by the member's edge that restamps it onto this lane. `error` parks the brief leg empty.

subject.description: GH #834: on `in_briefing`, the subject affinity briefed about -- its own hop key, carried through.

slots.description: GH #834: on `in_briefing`, the slots affinity was asked for, as the JSON list its hop carries.

finish_reason.description: On `in_answer`: how the completion ended (GH #843). Carried onto the `answer` it becomes, and `length` marks it `truncated`.

description.purpose: The context collector of one agent: it gathers what one round needs -- the turn(s) that opened it, the memory bundle, the brief, the tool round -- and hands all of it on, whole, to the curator, which owns the window (R-27-1, GH #889). Everything of a round leaves through ONE message on route 'curate' - and when the round has spent its iteration budget, that same seam leaves on 'answer' instead, so a runaway loop ends where it began. A round that lost a result does not park forever: when its last progress lies behind params.round_idle_ms, the next message that reaches the cell closes it - the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results with their tool_call_id kept, and the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. A user turn arriving while a round of its session is open is written and stamped deferred but starts NO second assembly: it rides with the next regular assembly (hop.round_deferred=1 on that arrival) - at most one open brain call per session. The rows of a round fall when the round ends (OR-KX-V2). A tool the dispatcher classified as ASYNC (hop.async_calls) opens no fan-in expectation at all: it is acknowledged on the spot under its own tool_call_id, and a bundle that asked for nothing else is filed as already fired when the turn is going to be answered anyway - either because the model spoke beside the bundle (the dispatcher already sent that sentence as the interim answer) or because a HANDOFF call took the turn with it (hop.handoff_calls: an advisor's event, an escalation opening a fresh turn). Neither, and the round stays OPEN (GH #372): the acknowledgement completes the fan-in, the regular guard fires and the seam re-enters the brain for the iteration the model has not spent, because a round that ends without a word ends in silence - a bare fire-and-forget call like `remember` used to leave the channel with no answer at all. Its result comes back later on the in_advice lane as an EVENT with a consult_id, is assembled like a turn and opens a FRESH round, so the follow-up reaches the channel in the agent's own voice; the ids of the advice turns in the round travel on 'curate' as system.consult.open, which is how a reply finds its way back to the right open question.
description.use_when: Between an agent's inbound surface and its LLM, in place of a persona cell that only injects a system prompt and a prep cell that only mints a turn id. Wire the eleven entry lanes and the six exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates the hive.
description.not_in_scope: No inference and no persona (identity is not context assembly, and the curate edge is ONE seam so an agent split can happen behind it later without re-cutting the collector). No tool fan-OUT: routing a tool_call to the right tool is a dispatcher's job, the collector only fans the results back in. No judgement about memory: the collector READS the recall bundle and nothing else. No window and no cap: what enters the model's window is the curator's (R-27-1, GH #889), and every item of a round leaves whole. No timer and no schedule of the template's own anywhere: the in_round_sweep lane is an OCCASION a parent tree may provide, and a sweep that finds nothing stale emits nothing. No classification of the async class: the dispatcher declares it and this cell obeys the marker. No rendering of an advisor event: what arrives on in_advice enters the round as its text, and the correlation ids leave as raw data. No fold: turning a round into prose is a lane this cell does not have.
description.emits_meaning: route cstore: store ops of the current step (hop.phase carries the state, hop.turn_id correlates the turn; both are promoted to context by the edge). route recall: the memory requests of this hive - one ambient request per turn (hop.memory_call_id empty) and one per memory_recall tool call (hop.memory_call_id = the tool_call_id, hop.recall_window_from / recall_window_to = the time range the MODEL asked for, GH #78). Both travel the same edge, so every key is always present and empty rather than absent. route brief: the brief leg's request (GH #834) - one tool_call {subject, channel, slots} to the member's affinity about context.counterpart, under a call id derived from the turn and the subject, hop.turn_id the turn; raised once per turn beside the ambient recall, only with params.brief_slots set and a counterpart in context. route curate: THE round, whole (GH #889) - messages[] the turn(s) that opened it followed by the tool round and, with params.memory_tier set, the ambient recall bundle as a synthetic memory_recall tool_call/tool_result pair at the end of it (GH #278: evidence of THIS round, under a call id derived from the bundle itself), then the brief pair; nothing of an earlier round. system carries the revocation of system.memory - the empty leaf on the fixed path recall plus the $replace marker, and no bundle data at all - system.consult (the raw correlation ids of the advice turns in the round, empty when there are none), system.instructions.mode/peer and system.roster; hop.iter the loop counter for the next call, hop.round_capped / partial the iteration cap, hop.round_stale=1 when the round was closed by the idle exit (a synthetic result travels in place of each lost one; a late real result wins over its stand-in), hop.round_deferred=1 when deferred turns ride in this round (their rows are dropped in the same multi-send); the marks of the removed caps and budget projection (window_dropped, window_capped, round_dropped, memory_capped, tokens_*, curate_*) stay, zero. route answer: the brain's final turn on its way out - OR, with hop.round_capped=1, the assembled round of a round that reached params.max_iter and will not ask again; either way the round's rows are dropped in the same multi-send (OR-KX-V2). An incomplete fan-in and a lost guard race emit NOTHING (empty multi-send, terminal by design). Since 4.4.0: the `curate` route carries `tool_scope` (the session's scope, absent without one) and `hop.scope_changed`, and every assembly writes `system.roster` and `system.instructions.peer`, empty when there is no participant or no peer turn.
description.consumes_meaning: The entry lanes, each named by hop.route on the port edge: in_turn (an inbound user turn), in_advice (an advisor's result or its question back, correlated by context.consult_id - the same chain as in_turn, filed under role 'advice' and opening a fresh round), in_bundle (the memory hive's bundle - the ambient leg of the turn, or the result of a memory_recall call when context.memory_call_id is set), in_briefing (affinity's answer to the brief leg, or its error as hop.brief_outcome='error' - an empty leg; the pack reaches the brain as a synthetic affinity_brief tool pair and its system slots are dropped, GH #834), in_calls (the assistant tool_call turn from the dispatcher; hop.async_calls names the ids this fan-in must NOT wait for, hop.handoff_calls the subset of those whose call ends the turn - GH #372), in_tool (one tool result: every `tool_result` turn of its `messages[]`, filed under the call id each answers -- a result carries no `system` slot and no top-level body slot, GH #252), in_answer (the brain's final turn), in_round_sweep (a timer's or operator's stuck-round re-check, the other occasion for the idle exit - never scheduled by the collector). Lanes are read before phases, because a message arriving over a port edge carries whatever col_phase its chain left in context. Store replies are dispatched by (context.col_phase, hop.operation); hop.rows_affected on a guarded update decides who fires - exactly once per turn and exactly once per tool round. Since 4.4.0 (GH #845, #847): `in_turn` reads `context.tools_allow`/`context.tools_deny` (the channel's tool scope, kept in the `session` row; no other lane reads them) and `context.roster_add`/`context.roster_leave` (the legend of the channel); a turn of `origin: "peer"` is kept as role `peer` with its `speaker`/`speaker_ref`, never as the agent's own answer; `in_briefing` reads affinity's `who` beside the text.
examples: turn 3 of a session -> insert user turn -> read the session's rows -> leg-window of turn 3 alone -> gate -> guarded fire -> curate carries turn 3 and nothing of turns 1..2: what the model keeps of those is the curator's (GH #889)
2 parallel tool calls -> 1 assistant row + 2 tool rows -> the round is complete -> guarded update wins once -> curate carries the opening + assistant turn + both results with hop.iter incremented
a 100 KB tool result -> the round row keeps all of it and curate carries all of it; what the model's window can afford is the curator's (GH #889)
a model that keeps asking for tools -> at iter == params.max_iter the seam emits route 'answer' with hop.round_capped=1 and everything collected so far, instead of a ninth brain call

params.memory_tier=0 -> the turn also fires a recall request; the bundle arrives on in_bundle, becomes the leg-memory row and enters the context window as the LAST tool_result of the round, answering a synthetic memory_recall call under a call id derived from the bundle itself (GH #278); system.memory carries only the revocation of the slot the bundle used to occupy

a tool dies mid-flight: 2 calls, 1 result, then silence -> the round parks; the next turn, the next result or an in_round_sweep request after params.round_idle_ms closes it - the missing call gets a synthetic 'tool result lost' result under its own tool_call_id, and the round fires regularly with hop.round_stale=1

a user turn arrives while a round runs -> it is written, stamped deferred, and starts NO second assembly (one open brain call per session, the telephone model); the next regular assembly carries it with hop.round_deferred=1 and drops its rows in the same multi-send

the brain asks for memory itself: a tool_call 'memory_recall' with {query, window_from, window_to} -> the dispatcher routes it by hop.tool_name like any other tool -> in_memory_call -> route 'recall' with the window as recall_window_from/_to and the call id as memory_call_id -> the bundle returns on in_bundle and becomes the tool_result of that call -> the round completes and re-enters the brain through the same seam
the same call with no memory wired anywhere -> unroutable, and the round ends in the idle exit of GH #103 rather than waiting forever

a bundle of one consult_cogny call with hop.async_calls='c1' AND a sentence beside it -> the assistant row is written as fired=1 and c1 is answered on the spot with 'handed to the async lane' -> no round is open, no sweep finds one, and the turn is over with the interim answer the dispatcher sent

the same bundle with NO text beside it and hop.handoff_calls empty (GH #372) -> the row stays OPEN, the acknowledgement completes the fan-in, the guard fires and the brain gets the iteration it has not spent -- bounded by params.max_iter, which leaves on route 'answer' with hop.round_capped=1 when it is spent

a bare escalate_to_deep call, no text, hop.handoff_calls='e1' -> filed as fired=1 like the first example: the answer comes from the turn the escalation opens, so this round is over without a word of its own
the same bundle plus a web_search c2 -> the assistant row stays open, c1 is acknowledged at once and the round completes as soon as c2 answers

the advisor answers hours later: in_advice with context.consult_id='k-7' -> an 'advice' turn is written, the memory leg fires like on any turn, the gate closes and the seam hands the curator a FRESH round that verbalises the result in the channel
the advisor asks back instead: the same lane, the same id -> the round carries the question and system.consult.open=['k-7'], so the next consult call can pass that id and the advisor keeps one thread
